title: Coixol attenuates osteoclastogenesis and ovariectomy-induced bone loss via the HIF-1alpha-mediated suppression of NF-kappaB signaling.
authors: Shi, Shu-Wen; Fu, Yi-Fei; Wu, Xian; Wang, Lei-Sheng; Zhang, Zhen-Yu; Luo, Zi-Xin; Wu, Jun-Jie; Yuan, Zheng-Dong; Nie, Hao; Zhang, Ke-Yue; Ti, Hui-Bo; Hu, Hai-Ting; Qian, Yi-Qing; Wang, Xin-Chen; Yao, Xing-Chen; Peng, Tao; Li, Xia; Yuan, Feng-Lai; Ye, Jun-Xing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Coixol通过HIF-1alpha抑制NF-kappaB信号通路影响破骨细胞生成与骨质疏松，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis is a common metabolic bone disease characterized by an imbalance in bone remodeling, which leads to elevated bone resorption due to enhanced osteoclastic activity. Current anti-resorptive therapies are limited by adverse effects and suboptimal efficacy. Coixol, a natural compound derived from the traditional edible plant Coix lacryma-jobi L., exhibits anti-inflammatory properties. However, its role in osteoporosis remains unclear. METHODS: The effects of coixol on osteoclast formation and function during receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANKL)-induced osteoclastogenesis were examined in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Differentiation was evaluated using tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase staining and F-actin ring formation assays, whereas bone resorption activity was quantified using pit formation assays. The expression levels of osteoclast-associated markers (NFATc1, CTSK, and MMP9) and hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1alpha) were assessed using reverse transcription quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction and Western blot assays. In vivo efficacy in an ovariectomized mouse model was determined using micro-computed tomography and histomorphometric analyses. RESULTS: Coixol dose-dependently inhibited osteoclast differentiation, disrupted F-actin ring formation, and decreased bone resorption activity, and these activities were accompanied by the downregulation of key osteoclastogenic genes and proteins. Under normoxic conditions, coixol increased HIF-1alpha protein levels. In ovariectomized mice, coixol significantly attenuated bone loss, improved trabecular bone microstructure, and suppressed osteoclast activity. CONCLUSION: Coixol likely inhibits osteoclast formation and bone resorption in vitro and in vivo by activating HIF-1alpha and suppressing nuclear factor-kappa B pathway signaling. These findings suggest that coixol, acting through an HIF-1alpha-mediated mechanism, could be a potential natural therapeutic agent for osteoporosis.
abstract_zh: 背景：骨质疏松症是一种常见的代谢性骨病，其特征是骨重塑失衡，导致破骨细胞活性增强进而引起骨吸收升高。目前的抗骨吸收疗法受限于不良反应和疗效欠佳。Coixol是一种源自传统食用植物薏苡（Coix lacryma-jobi L.）的天然化合物，具有抗炎特性。然而，其在骨质疏松症中的作用尚不明确。方法：在骨髓来源巨噬细胞中，检测了coixol在核因子κB受体活化因子配体（RANKL）诱导的破骨细胞生成过程中对破骨细胞形成和功能的影响。通过抗酒石酸酸性磷酸酶染色和F-actin环形成实验评估分化，而骨吸收活性则通过骨陷窝形成实验进行定量。使用逆转录定量实时聚合酶链反应和Western blot实验评估破骨细胞相关标志物（NFATc1、CTSK和MMP9）及缺氧诱导因子1-α（HIF-1α）的表达水平。在去卵巢小鼠模型中，通过显微计算机断层扫描和组织形态计量学分析确定体内疗效。结果：Coixol剂量依赖性地抑制破骨细胞分化，破坏F-actin环形成，并降低骨吸收活性，这些作用伴随着关键破骨细胞生成基因和蛋白质的下调。在常氧条件下，coixol增加了HIF-1α蛋白水平。在去卵巢小鼠中，coixol显著减轻骨丢失，改善小梁骨微结构，并抑制破骨细胞活性。结论：Coixol可能通过激活HIF-1α和抑制核因子-κB通路信号，在体外和体内抑制破骨细胞形成和骨吸收。这些发现表明，coixol通过HIF-1α介导的机制发挥作用，可能成为骨质疏松症的潜在天然治疗剂。
